name: kill
description: The kill() system call sends a signal to a specified process or process group. If pid is positive, it sends the signal to that process; other values of pid target process groups or all processes. It can also be used to check for the existence of a process without sending a signal if sig is 0.

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description: The process ID to send the signal to. Positive for a specific process, 0 for the process group of the caller, -1 for all processes (with permissions), or less than -1 for a specific process group.

parameters.name: sig
parameters.description: The signal number to send. If 0, no signal is sent, but checks for existence and permissions are performed.

return_value.success: Returns zero if at least one signal was sent
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The calling process does not have permission to send the signal to any of the target processes
The target process or process group does not exist

bugs: In Linux 2.6 up to and including 2.6.7, when sending signals to a process group, kill() failed with EPERM if the caller lacked permission for any member, though the signal was still delivered to permissible processes.
versions: POSIX.1-2001, SVr4, 4.3BSD; Linux with permission rules adopted in 1.3.78
